picks.title: MHRA 2030 Strategy to modernise patient-centred regulation for the era of AI and personalised medicines
picks.excerpt: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has set out ambitious plans to translate cutting-edge scientific and technological innovation into better health outcomes for patients across all four nations of the UK, in its 2030 Strategy published today.
picks.rationale: This is a primary regulator release. The UK medicines and devices regulator published its 2030 strategy, which resets how AI and personalised medicines are regulated for patients across the UK.

picks.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
picks.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in huma
picks.rationale: In this Nature paper, AI measures brown-fat activity on clinical scans at scale. That links it to metabolic and psychiatric outcomes and surfaces existing drugs that could be repurposed, so it is clinical-cohort work with named disease endpoints.

picks.title: Bradford skin cancer waiting times cut by new AI technology
picks.excerpt: Clinic can now see more patients and get results faster thanks to new scanning technology.
picks.rationale: An NHS skin-cancer clinic in Bradford now uses AI scanning in routine care and has cut its waiting times. Patients are already getting faster results.

picks.title: Electronic health record developer adherence to federal AI risk transparency requirements - npj Digital Medicine
picks.excerpt: We evaluated electronic health record developer compliance with federal transparency requirements for AI-enabled predictive decision support interventions. Developers are required to publicly report on risk analysis, mitigation, governance, and on eight other attributes. Across 35 developers, report
picks.rationale: The study audits 35 EHR developers against the federal rules requiring them to disclose AI risk for decision-support tools. It shows how well the rule clinicians rely on is actually being followed.

picks.title: Lobbyists and trade groups fight to shape how states regulate medical AI
picks.excerpt: Lobbying groups for doctors and hospitals and trade groups are working behind the scenes on how to regulate AI in medicine.
picks.rationale: STAT reports how the AMA, hospital groups and trade groups are pushing state rules on autonomous clinical AI. Those rules will decide what AI can do without a physician.

alternates.title: Johns Hopkins Medicine taps OpenEvidence to bring AI into medical education, clinical care
alternates.excerpt: Johns Hopkins Medicine is teaming up with OpenEvidence to advance the use of artificial intelligence in medical education and clinical care.
alternates.rationale: An academic medical center is partnering with an AI vendor, but no concrete change to care has been announced yet. It is the first alternate.

alternates.title: AI, Tech Leaders Are Lobbying Trump Health Officials in a Government-Run Chat Room - KFF Health News
alternates.excerpt: A Slack workspace managed by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has served as an extraordinary war room for AI industry insiders and Trump administration officials to launch a rapid campaign aimed at persuading Americans to manage their healthcare and medical records on apps.
alternates.rationale: An investigation into industry lobbying of CMS. It overlaps in theme with the STAT lobbying pick and is older, so it is the second alternate.

dedup.note: The pool had 17 candidates, no clusters and 2 history_match tags, both 'related'. Dropped as running-story commentary: the MedCity surgical-robots piece (tagged 'related' to the 10-11 Healthcare Dive story on FDA prioritizing surgical-robot guidance) is opinion on hospital readiness for FDA draft guidance and reports no new FDA action of its own. Dropped as commentary or op-ed: MedCity cognitive decline (tagged 'related' to the 10-09 epilepsy-EHR paper but a different topic, and opinion only); MedCity agentic-AI piece; STAT doctor op-ed on AI and costs; KFF 'Who gets left behind' podcast; KFF Monitor digest. Dropped as reactions: Radiology Business 'physicians fire back at HHS secretary' (reactions to remarks from 10-01, also dropped 10-14). Dropped as minor: Brainomix e-Lung adding patient input (an extension of an existing study); MHRA DMHT working-group page (a background publication from the same outlet as the stronger MHRA 2030 Strategy pick); Nature 'Hidden signals in sleep' (news feature with no specific clinical deployment). Alternates are Johns Hopkins/OpenEvidence (partnership with no care change yet) and KFF Health News on CMS Slack lobbying (thematic overlap with the STAT pick). Content checks: the MHRA 2030 Strategy (MHRA, 10-14) is a different release from the DHSC endorsement of the NHS AI Commission published 10-14, which was dated 10-06. The STAT state-lobbying story is not a follow-up to the Utah pilots or the JAMA regulation precedent piece. The npj EHR transparency audit is a new study. Diversity: nature.com 2, gov.uk 1, bbc 1, statnews 1, for 4 distinct outlets. No pick touches biosecurity or gain-of-function.
